[{"type":"GeneralTitle","content":"Bachelor of Science in Computer Science","groupId":"3fcc5f03-9e2e-4dc8-adb0-0195908b29e4","position":0,"area":"General"},{"type":"GeneralText","content":"

Students must complete a minimum of 120 units with a Pacific cumulative and major/program grade point average of 2.0 in order to earn the Bachelor of Science in Computer Science.

","groupId":"8d0be799-fe27-43b7-9707-0195908b29e4","position":1,"area":"General"},{"type":"GeneralTitle","content":"General Education Requirements","groupId":"4118b14c-9cac-47ed-8696-01959090d3c8","position":2,"area":"General"},{"type":"GeneralText","content":"

For more details, see General Education

Minimum 28 units and 9 courses that include the following requirements.

","groupId":"244d313a-3724-40d8-971b-01959090d3c8","position":3,"area":"General"},{"type":"GeneralTitle","content":"CORE Requirement","groupId":"b102cf6b-b6ca-4453-a33c-01959090d3c8","position":4,"area":"General"},{"type":"GeneralText","content":"

Notes:

1) CORE Seminars cannot be taken for Pass/No Credit. 

2) Transfer students with 28 or more transfer credits taken after high school are exempt from both CORE seminars. 

","groupId":"33d977f0-d129-4694-9b81-01959090d3c8","position":5,"area":"General"},{"type":"GeneralTitle","content":"Breadth Requirement (7 courses, at least 3 units each)","groupId":"c32c17ee-0c36-4965-82c3-01959090d3c8","position":6,"area":"General"},{"type":"GeneralText","content":"

Note: No more than 2 courses from a single discipline can be used to meet the Breadth Requirement.

","groupId":"441e99cf-12c6-4efc-a8fd-01959090d3c8","position":7,"area":"General"},{"type":"GeneralTitle","content":"Diversity and Inclusion Requirement","groupId":"3d6b1d4f-bace-4a11-b400-019590919a2f","position":8,"area":"General"},{"type":"GeneralText","content":"

All students must complete Diversity and Inclusion coursework (at least 3 units)

Note: Diversity and Inclusion courses can also be used to meet the breadth category requirements, or major or minor requirements.

","groupId":"9b105453-a9de-4135-b5c4-019590919a2f","position":9,"area":"General"},{"type":"GeneralTitle","content":"Fundamental Skills","groupId":"76ea2b99-d033-441e-a718-0195909286db","position":10,"area":"General"},{"type":"GeneralText","content":"

Students must demonstrate competence in:

Writing

Quantitative Analysis (Math)

Note: Failure to satisfy the fundamental skills requirements by the end of four semesters of full-time study at the University is grounds for academic disqualification

","groupId":"ef77199c-6616-40c9-8221-0195909286db","position":11,"area":"General"},{"type":"GeneralTitle","content":"Major Requirements","groupId":"8a5c4b9b-a841-44f4-be6d-0195909db72c","position":12,"area":"General"},{"type":"GeneralText","content":"

Notes:

1) 15 units in mathematics and 8 units in laboratory science. COMP 047, COMP 147 and ECPE 127count as mathematics units.

2) Students who transfer in with 28 or more units are exempt from taking IDEA 010 and IDEA 020.

3) Students complete their degree with 17 additional units of approved upper division Computing Electives, beyond the Computer Science Core courses, which students select in consultation with their academic advisor. These courses may include 100-level COMP courses and no more than one course from BENG 175, ECPE 172, ECPE 173, ECPE 174, and EMGT 162. Up to four units of ENGR 182or COMP 187 may be substituted for upper division computing elective units.
